nodes.name: Hydrothermal NiMoO4 synthesis
nodes.procedure: NiMoO4·xH2O nanowires were first synthesized on NF through a simple hydrothermal method. 1 mmol Ni(NO3)2·6H2O and 1 mmol Na2MoO4·2H2O were dissolved in 20 mL DI water and stirred for 30 min, the obtained solution was transferred to a 50 ml Teflon-lined stainless-steel autoclave with the pretreated NF (2 cm × 3 cm), then maintained at 150°C for 6 h. After cooling down room temperature, the NiMoO4·xH2O/NF was taken out and carefully cleaned and dried.

nodes.name: Electrochemical reconstruction to R-NiFeOOH@SO4
nodes.procedure: Electrochemical CV activation was manipulated from 0.2 to 0.8 V vs. Hg/HgO for 20 cycles at a scan rate of 20 mV s^-1 to induce structural reconstruction of NiMoO4·xH2O@Fe,S, generating reactive R-NiFeOOH@SO4. The load of R-NiFeOOH@SO4 on the Ni foam is determined to be about 6.85 mg cm^-2.

nodes.evidence_snippet: After activation, the Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) surface area of R-NiFeOOH@SO4 increases...

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows diffraction peaks of initial NiMoO4·xH2O disappear completely in R-NiFeOOH@SO4 with no NiOOH peaks due to lower crystallinity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The powder X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern reveals that the diffraction peak of initial NiMoO4·xH2O in R-NiFeOOH@SO4 completely disappears, while no related diffraction peak of NiOOH is detected due to lower crystallinity.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS confirms almost complete removal of Mo and homogeneous distribution of Ni, Fe, S, O throughout R-NiFeOOH@SO4 nanorods.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In addition, energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) confirms the almost complete removal of elemental Mo from all catalysts, and the elements of Ni, Fe, S, and O are distributed homogeneously...

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES confirms large-scale Mo dissolution with Fe 9.88 at% and S 6.6 at% in R-NiFeOOH@SO4.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The inductively coupled plasma-optical emission spectrometry (ICP-OES) results further substantiate the large-scale Mo dissolution in R-NiFeOOH@SO4, and the content of Fe and S as modulator was determined to be 9.88 and 6.6 at%...

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman reveals conversion of catalysts to oxyhydroxides at anodic potentials with modulated Ni-site redox in NiMoO4·xH2O@Fe,S.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In situ Raman spectra further reveal the conversion of the catalysts to oxyhydroxides at anodic potentials, in which NiMoO4·xH2O@Fe,S has a modulated Ni-site redox and favorable Mo dissolution.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS Ni 2p spectra shift to lower binding energies for NiMoO4·xH2O@Fe and @Fe,S relative to NiMoO4·xH2O; post-CV activation R-NiFeOOH@SO4 shows smaller negative shift (-0.24 eV) and higher Ni oxidation state; O 1s M-O signal positive shift (0.4 eV max for R-NiFeOOH@SO4); Fe 2p shifts to higher binding energy indicating higher oxidation state; S 2p transforms to SO4^2- characteristic peaks.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ni 2p spectra of NiMoO4·xH2O@Fe and NiMoO4·xH2O@Fe,S significantly shift to lower binding energies relative to NiMoO4·xH2O... such a negative shift between NiMoO4·xH2O@Fe,S and R-NiFeOOH@SO4 is smaller (-0.24 eV)... the M-O offset of R-NiFeOOH@SO4 is more significant (0.4 eV)... the S 2p signal of R-NiFeOOH@SO4 is completely transformed into oxidized S species, which corresponds to the characteristic signal peak of sulfate (SO4^2-).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge XANES: post-activation absorption edges shift lower, R-NiFeOOH@SO4 shows least shift/highest energy position; Fe K-edge: lower average oxidation state in NiMoO4·xH2O@Fe,S vs @Fe, shifts higher post-activation in R-NiFeOOH@SO4; S K-edge confirms SO4^2- form in R-NiFeOOH@SO4.
nodes.evidence_snippet: After CV activation, the absorption edges of all catalysts shift to the lower energy, in which R-NiFeOOH@SO4 has a lower degree of shift and is located at the highest energy position... Compared to NiMoO4·xH2O@Fe, the Fe K-edge XANES also displays a lower average Fe oxidation state in NiMoO4·xH2O@Fe,S, which shifts to the higher energy for R-NiFeOOH@SO4.

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-EXAFS Ni K-edge shows Ni-O (1.59 Å) and Ni-M (2.72 Å) shells; reduced Ni-O coordination number indicates oxygen vacancies in @Fe,S; enhanced Ni-O intensity post-activation in R-NiFeOOH@SO4 confirms vacancy refilling.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Two characteristic peaks at 1.59 and 2.72 Å in Ni K-edge FT-EXAFS spectra can be ascribed to the Ni-O first shell and the Ni-M second shell... After CV activation, the peak intensity of the Ni-O path of R-NiFeOOH@SO4 is enhanced...
